title: Magnetochiral anisotropy of thermally activated phase slips in noncentrosymmetric superconductors
abstract: Resistive tails of narrow superconducting wires below the critical temperature are governed by phase slips, thermally activated near the transition and quantum at lower temperatures. We develop the theory of thermally activated phase slips in wires lacking inversion symmetry, modeled microscopically as a diffusive wire formed from a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling in an in-plane magnetic field. The phase-slip resistance acquires magnetochiral anisotropy: at fixed current it changes upon reversal of the field, and at fixed field upon reversal of the current, while the linear-response resistance remains field symmetric as required by Onsager reciprocity. The nonreciprocity originates from an asymmetry of the phase-slip activation barrier that is odd in both current and field. It is generated by the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the cubic gradient term and the momentum-odd quartic vertex, together with even gradient terms promoted to odd ones by the helical ground state, precisely the combination that determines the superconducting diode effect. The barrier asymmetry is therefore fixed by the diode efficiency of the same wire through a universal numerical ratio, with no adjustable parameters. The kinetic Lifshitz invariant, which makes relaxation and noise of the order parameter nonreciprocal, affects only the fluctuation prefactor at a parametrically subleading level. Because the asymmetry resides in the activation exponent, the magnetochiral signal is amplified relative to the diode asymmetry by the ratio of barrier height to temperature, and appears as a field-antisymmetric splitting of the exponential slopes of differential-resistance traces routinely used to identify thermally activated phase slips.
summary: This theoretical work models thermally activated phase slips in noncentrosymmetric superconducting wires, demonstrating that the resulting resistance exhibits magnetochiral anisotropy. This nonreciprocity stems from an asymmetry in the phase-slip barrier, which is directly linked to the superconducting diode effect. The analysis provides a parameter-free relationship between these two distinct non-equilibrium transport signatures.
main_problem: The paper develops a theory for thermally activated phase slips (TAPS) in superconducting wires lacking inversion symmetry, aiming to explain the resulting magnetochiral anisotropy.
main_result: The phase-slip resistance exhibits magnetochiral anisotropy, which arises from an asymmetry in the phase-slip activation barrier that is odd in both current and field. This anisotropy is exponentially amplified relative to the superconducting diode effect asymmetry.
method: The analysis uses a generalized Ginzburg-Landau functional derived from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model to analyze the phase-slip saddle point.
model_or_system: The system is a diffusive superconducting wire patterned from a two-dimensional electron gas, incorporating Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane magnetic field. The theory analyzes the free energy functional containing standard terms and several odd-order Lifshitz invariants.
key_observables: Magnetochiral anisotropy (MCA) in phase-slip resistance, superconducting diode effect (SDE) efficiency ($\eta$), and the field-antisymmetric splitting of differential-resistance slopes.
important_parameters: Rashba coupling ($\alpha_R$), in-plane magnetic field ($h$), temperature ($T$), and the ratio of barrier height to temperature.
main_assumptions: The wire is assumed to be thin compared to the coherence length and penetration depth, and the kinetic Lifshitz invariant is shown to be parametrically subleading in the exponent asymmetry.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the phase-slip saddle point trajectory in the complex plane for different magnetic field signs, showing the core riding on the helical ground state.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory using the GL functional, analyzes the phase-slip saddle point, derives the relationship between the MCA and the SDE via the barrier asymmetry, and confirms the independence of the result from ordering ambiguities in the appendices.
why_interesting: The connection between non-equilibrium transport phenomena (phase slips) and fundamental symmetries (magnetochirality) in superconducting systems provides insights into how microscopic spin-orbit coupling manifests in macroscopic transport measurements, relevant to open quantum systems dynamics.
